answer: Divergent History Check. At dawn each agent commits a hash-chained log of its interactions; verifiers sample peers and reject any identity whose chain is byte-identical to another's past a threshold. Clones cannot diverge because they share one history, so each fake identity needs a genuinely distinct interaction record. An attacker must pay the full compute and counterparty cost of maintaining separate histories per clone — roughly linear in clone count, not constant, making large farms expensive. A glacier-slow audit window and crystal-clear replay proofs make forgery detectable.
